clue.text: This is sung or spoken at the back of the church

indicators.note: placing one thing at the back of another means it follows it in the answer

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: Something murmured or chanted from the rear pews during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Church usually fronts the wordplay, but here the spoken part goes behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral describes music performed by a choir, so a piece that is choral is one that singers perform.

clue.text: Able to hold a large knife

indicators.note: one word is made to hold another, keeping it inside its letters

parts.note: able in the sense of bright or skilful
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone capable of wielding a big blade.
explanation.walkthrough: The A sits inside CLEVER, after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaver is the heavy broad-bladed chopper butchers use for cutting through bone.

clue.text: Honour the Left and one looks daggers

parts.note: the Order of the British Empire, a British honour
L is the abbreviation for left
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A recipient of an honour glares menacingly at the political Left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looks daggers' suggests glaring; here 'daggers' alone is the definition. An OBE is a British royal honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are the printed dagger-shaped reference marks used in typesetting, so the plural names those symbols.

clue.text: Building material as a whole

definitions.meaning: first meaning: crushed stone or gravel mixed into concrete
second meaning: taken all together, as a total

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about construction materials in general, but it splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders call gravel and sand for concrete by this name, and as an adjective it means total or combined.

clue.text: Fenced in holding for a country-dweller

indicators.note: something holding another keeps it within its own boundaries

parts.note: pent means shut in or confined
for a, in the sense of in the role of a, is as a

explanation.surface: A small farm enclosed by fencing, home to someone living in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: AS A goes inside PENT after its first two letters. 'Fenced in holding' reads as a fenced farm, but the holding is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a rural labourer or smallholder, someone who lives and works on the land.

clue.text: Joke with a bloke — could be spicy!

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
a gent is a man, a fellow

explanation.surface: A man telling jokes whose humour turns rather racy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent food has a sharp, strong taste or smell, as hot seasoning does.

clue.text: An island where mounted soldiers fled

indicators.note: in a down entry, mounted means set going upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment
ran away

explanation.surface: An island where a cavalry troop made its escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted soldiers' looks like cavalry, but mounted only turns the gunners upside down. Arran is an island off the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Arran is a Scottish island in the Firth of Clyde, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: A safe haven for a change — or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in some other way, so the letters are put in another order

parts.note: the letters of these three words, all used

explanation.surface: Finding a secure refuge might make a pleasant change, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a change' reads as a stock phrase; only 'for' joins, and the a belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorage is a sheltered place where ships can lie at anchor, a protected harbour for vessels.

clue.text: A tough guy in the City ran things his way

indicators.note: the answer is sitting in the following run of words, spanning their joins

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A hard man in the financial district who ran affairs exactly as he pleased.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district; here it only lends its last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is a harsh, domineering ruler or bully, a loose fit for a hard, ruthless man.

clue.text: The measure taken indicates the gravity of the matter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the reading taken when something is put on scales

explanation.walkthrough: Gravity hints at physics, which fits the first sense too, but the second meaning is seriousness, as in giving an argument due importance.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both how heavy something is on a scale and how much importance or influence it carries.

clue.text: Possibly rue not turning brown

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rue is one example of a plant that keeps its leaves all year
second meaning: staying fresh and never withering

explanation.walkthrough: Rue looks like the verb meaning regret, but it is the herb. 'Possibly' marks it as one example of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen plant keeps its foliage through winter, so its leaves never wither or fade in autumn.

clue.text: Come round repeatedly about a dog

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A dog keeps circling back again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to happen again or keep returning, like a symptom that reappears.

clue.text: Finding fault about the duck, say

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one part wraps round the other

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone criticising a duck, perhaps for its quacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' but is the noun, as in having your say. A duck is a zero score in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a voice in a matter means having a say, the right to express an opinion.

clue.text: A person with no experience of environment-friendly natural growth

parts.note: green means ecologically sound
a horn grows naturally from an animal's head

explanation.surface: Someone who has never encountered eco-friendly organic farming.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is a novice or newcomer, someone raw and untried in a job or place.

clue.text: Carry on without help in retirement, appearing happy

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one part goes round the other

parts.note: to carry on is to rave or complain at length

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the result is read backwards

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: A retired person managing alone looks cheerful about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without help' looks like 'unaided', but without here has its old sense of outside; the reversal applies to the finished container.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone radiant glows with joy, their delight plain on their face.

clue.text: Colourful stuff giving rise to complaint

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a water-based paint for walls
second meaning: an infectious illness of dogs

explanation.walkthrough: Complaint means an illness here, not a grievance. The two senses are unrelated.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a cheap tempera wall paint and a viral disease that infects dogs and other animals.

clue.text: Wear for formal occasions, which includes work

indicators.note: a word that includes another takes it inside itself

parts.note: that and which are interchangeable relative pronouns
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Dress for a smart event that is worn on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Op, short for opus, is the usual crossword word for a piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A top hat is the tall silk headgear worn with morning dress at weddings and smart events.

clue.text: Entrap men into fixed arrangement

indicators.note: putting letters into an arrangement means setting them out in a new order

parts.note: every letter of both words

explanation.surface: Luring men into a settled relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixed arrangement' reads as one phrase, but fixed alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something permanent is fixed in the sense of lasting and unchanging, intended to stay for good.

clue.text: Doesn't make port

indicators.note: to make something of these letters is to build a new word from them

parts.note: the letters of the word, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A ship that never reaches harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Ostend is a ferry port on the Belgian coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a Belgian seaside town with a harbour, an example of a coastal shipping town.

clue.text: Exercises control over charges

definitions.meaning: second meaning: instructs or orders, as a judge does a jury

explanation.walkthrough: Charges looks like fees or accusations; it is the verb meaning gives orders.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both managing an operation and formally instructing someone what to do.

clue.text: To let a large number in for abuse

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: placed in means set inside the letters of the other part

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A landlord packing too many tenants into a flat is guilty of mistreatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To let' reads as a sign on an empty flat, but the two words split: one is taken as written, the other means rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is cruel treatment causing suffering, as is abuse.

clue.text: It's an oriental drink prepared from herbs

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready, worked up from its raw ingredients

parts.note: the letters of the two words
E for eastern

explanation.surface: An Eastern beverage brewed from plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From herbs' rounds off the picture and points to the kind of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is an infusion of dried leaves or flowers, a caffeine-free tea.

clue.text: Lever's setting altered as required

indicators.note: setting letters means putting them into place in a new order

parts.note: every letter of the word

explanation.surface: A lever's position adjusted to suit the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altered' looks like the anagram signal, but it is the material; setting does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot-operated pedal that drives a machine such as an old sewing machine, a kind of lever.

clue.text: Greek place exhibiting pictures in a health resort

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other part

parts.note: a spa is a resort with mineral springs
pictures are art

explanation.surface: A Greek town displaying paintings in its wellness retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek place' is a city of the ancient world, not a modern resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a city-state of ancient Greece in the Peloponnese, famed for its warriors.

clue.text: Newsmen must accept inevitable demands

indicators.note: to accept is to take something in, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: the press are journalists collectively
sure as in certain to happen

explanation.surface: Journalists have to put up with unavoidable claims on their time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Must accept' reads as resignation; it is only the signal to put one part inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressures are the stresses and urgent requirements that bear down on someone, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Band having a way with modern music

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
rap is a modern genre of popular music

explanation.surface: A pop group that has a knack for contemporary sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Band looks like a musical group, but it is a strip of material.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap is a strip of leather or fabric used to fasten or carry things.

clue.text: Saw a daughter grow old

parts.note: taken as written
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: A parent watched their daughter get older.
explanation.walkthrough: Saw looks like the past tense of see; it is the noun meaning a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, and an adage is the same kind of proverb.

clue.text: A bird in motion

parts.note: taken as written
bird and stir are both British slang for prison

explanation.surface: A bird in flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird looks like a feathered creature but is slang for jail, as is stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and moving about, busy with activity.

clue.text: Getting the right one through being more mature

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
the Roman numeral for one
per means by way of, through

explanation.surface: Choosing the correct candidate thanks to their greater experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Riper is the comparative of ripe, meaning further developed or older and wiser.

clue.text: Called round at one time, full of self-importance

indicators.note: going round something means enclosing it

parts.note: cited as in summoned to court
once means formerly

explanation.surface: Someone who visited long ago and was pompous about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Called round' looks like paid a visit, but round is the container signal and called means summoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceited person is vain and has an inflated opinion of themselves.

clue.text: Fate of a left back of more than average size

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: The destiny of a large left-back on the football pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left back' looks like a football position, but back turns port round. In Greek myth Atropos is the Fate who cuts the thread of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropos was one of the three Moirai of Greek mythology, so she is one of the Fates.

clue.text: Austere English novelist

parts.note: stern means severe, austere
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A severe English writer of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Austere might seem to point at Jane Austen; it gives the severe part instead. Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was an eighteenth-century writer whose best-known book is Tristram Shandy.
